rationale: The client-contract check completed. Receipt 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db (exit 0, thirty events, no parse loss) resolves both comparisons: with RestoreCommittedLogs on, the isolated node won with two of the committed five votes and its client Apply returned success (comparison 0 violated, witness event index 27, minority_leader true, minority_apply_ok true), while the flag-off control could not produce a leader on that side at all (comparison 1 holds, evaluated event index 29, minority_leader false, minority_apply_ok false, with the majority side acknowledging its own write). That closes the client-contract half of this question: an acknowledgement can rest on a minority of the committed configuration. The run again produced no majority-side leader on the flagged side's behalf, so no FSM divergence or lost acknowledged entry was witnessed and the gap stays open on that point only. The configuration and election comparisons are unchanged.

investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership and it can win an election its committed configuration would forbid.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration, then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and check whether it wins with the smaller quorum while the majority side keeps a leader.

knowledge.statement: A node restarted with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs that keeps a stale, smaller configuration can acknowledge a client write while its support is a minority of the committed configuration: isolated together with one committed voter it became leader and its Apply completed, whereas the same restart without the flag produced no leader on that side and no acknowledgement.
knowledge.conditions: Committed configuration grown from three to five voters after the restarting node's snapshot; RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the node isolated together with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns, that partner also cut off from the majority side; two second apply timeout, bounded observation window, flag-off control in the same execution.

gaps.question: Does a leader elected with fewer votes than the committed configuration requires reproduce reliably, under which schedule and partition order, and does the committed configuration's majority side then diverge in committed entries?

interpretations.rationale: Three completed comparisons, each with its flag-off control, answer this question. Configuration: receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 15 - the node restarted from a log whose latest configuration is index 14 with five servers came back at configuration index 1 with three servers - control holding at evaluated event index 18 (index 14, five servers). Election: receipt abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 22 - isolated with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returned, the node became leader with reachable_votes 2 against committed_quorum 3, and the same run reports majority_side_leader true - control holding at evaluated event index 25. Client contract: receipt 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 27 - the isolated leader's Apply completed (minority_apply_ok true) while the flag-off control produced no leader there and no acknowledgement (comparison 1 holds, evaluated event index 29). Source: restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index before the startup scan at api.go:604-620, so AddVoter's later entry (api.go:994-1005) is never re-read and the node keeps the snapshot's three-server list; quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) then returns two, electSelf (raft.go:1999-2060) asks only that list, and the leader's commitment calculation (commitment.go:60-105) accepts the two matching indexes as a quorum, so the write is acknowledged against a majority of the stale configuration rather than of the committed one. The manoeuvre the runs needed - also cutting the single committed voter off from the majority side so requestVote's existing-leader guard (raft.go:1690-1700) does not refuse the vote - is an ordinary partition shape; the minority leadership reproduced in the two immediate-isolation executions and not in two settled-schedule executions, so the manifestation is schedule dependent while the decision and the acknowledgement are unrepaired by the library. Not witnessed: any FSM divergence or lost acknowledged entry, because no run produced a majority-side leader that wrote concurrently.
counterevidence: The flag-off controls in all three receipts keep the committed configuration, cannot win on the isolated side and do not acknowledge a write there.

Two settled-schedule executions did not produce the minority leadership, and the difference is explained by whether the isolated partner still heard the majority-side leader; no frequency or absence claim is made.
The redundant configuration re-checks in one earlier receipt were incomplete because two scenarios emit the same restart event name; they carry no new claim and are not used.
limitations: No FSM divergence or lost acknowledged entry is witnessed: in the client-contract run the majority side had no leader, so only one side wrote.
Observed windows are bounded (five second election window, two second apply timeout, two second heal settle), so no occurrence-rate or absence bound is established.
The scenario restarts the former leader of an enlarged cluster with an added-voter change; other roles, change types and chain orders are not explored.

7da03e78394f41fdad540ae0824ec2a6-gap-1.explanation: Election and acknowledgement are resolved by complete comparisons (abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407 witness index 22 with control 25; 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db witness index 27 with control 29). Reproduction depends on whether the single committed voter on the isolated side still hears the majority-side leader, because requestVote refuses candidates while a leader is known (raft.go:1690-1700); with immediate isolation it reproduced in both executions, with the settled schedule it did not. Entry-level divergence still has no witness: no run produced a majority-side leader writing concurrently with the minority leader, so this part of the gap stays open.

interpretations.joint_history: Three complete executions of the same five-voter scenario over identical stores, sizes and snapshot timing supply the three comparisons: b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 (configuration loss and its control, both reporting index 1 with three servers against expected 14 with five on the flagged side and 14 with five on the control), abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407 (election and its control), and 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db (client acknowledgement and its control). Each receipt built its own cluster and stores and is a complete history in itself; only the comparison declarations and event names differ between them, and the configuration values agree across all three, so none is a fragment of another.
